structured_output.analysis: The budget is 403/128 bits per weight, and the best grid iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e) is already within about 2e-4 bits per weight of it, so any per-layer upgrade has to be paid for by a downgrade. For the layers where loss is concentrated, the only records I have show that dropping one more of them to int2 costs several times what an upgrade gains. For example, 27.gate_proj measures 0.0234424 at rht_gptq_int2 against 0.00498703 at rht_gptq_int3. So a bit-neutral swap backed by records is not available yet. Last round's option proposals were refused only because their rationales quoted a rounded KL. I am resubmitting the same option ideas without unsupported numbers. Changing act_order or damp does not change the stored bits, so these grids stay within budget.

proposals.name: opt_act_order_v2
proposals.rationale: This keeps the per-layer grid of iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e) and sets act_order=true for the GPTQ-family layers. Stored bits are unchanged. The worst layers have very spread-out activations: 27.up_proj has activation kurtosis 1090.09 (E24beed188b6a) and channel absmax ratio 65.2425 (E3c29dce14bae). Quantizing the most active columns first should lower GPTQ error on layers like these.

proposals.name: opt_damp_high_v2
proposals.rationale: This keeps the iso_3.15 grid (E514ab09c524e) and sets damp=0.05. Stored bits are unchanged. Calibration is small (8x512), and activation kurtosis is extreme: 1090.09 in 27.gate_proj (E5aee24c5494a) and 324.063 in 2.up_proj (Ecbd8d8937247). Stronger damping regularizes the Hessian, which may reduce overfitting on low-bit layers such as 14.down_proj at rht_gptq_int2 (E4c3f9b73e065).

proposals.name: opt_act_order_damp_high
proposals.rationale: This combines act_order=true with damp=0.05 on the iso_3.15 grid (E514ab09c524e) at the same stored bits. It targets layers with outlier activation channels, such as 27.up_proj with outlier_channels 0.00976562 (E1cdf4d37dde6) and 3.up_proj with activation kurtosis 241.283 (Eb1b68d163774), where reordering and stronger damping may help together.

proposals.name: opt_damp_low_v2
proposals.rationale: This keeps the iso_3.15 grid (E514ab09c524e) and sets damp=0.002, so the GPTQ error compensation follows the calibration Hessian more closely. Stored bits are unchanged. It brackets the damp=0.05 proposal so the measured whole-recipe KL shows which direction helps the int3 MLP layers, such as 1.up_proj (E0564bc6ad1eb) and 2.up_proj (E9baa10763ebe).
